rationale: Coptic ϩⲁϣ-ϩⲱ likely from a doubling-root meaning 'multitude, great quantity.' Recurs four times on this page (lines 1-4, 14) as the structuring noun for cataloguing sin-categories: 'the abundance of lawlessness,' 'the abundance of his corpses,' 'the abundance of his fornication.' Captures the quantitative-intensifying register.

Compound: ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ (Lyc. word, in glossary) + ⲉⲧ-ϯ-ⲁⲥⲉ (relative + give-wound). The third great sin-category in this kephalaion that wounds the cross of the Light. Direct correspondential rendering: speech that does the act of wounding — ⲁⲥⲉ from ⲥⲁϣ/ⲁⲥⲉ 'blow, stripe, wound.' Distinguished from ordinary speech (ⲥⲉϫⲉ) by the wounding action.

Lycopolitan particle/noun + directional ⲁ- functioning as 'toward' in the doublet ⲃⲉ ⲁⲡⲧⲱⲛϩ̄ / ⲃⲉ ⲁⲡⲙⲟⲩ 'way toward life / way toward death.' Possibly Lyc. variant of a movement/direction noun; awaits parallels for definitive identification. Confidence low.

Greek κατά + Lyc. -ⲣⲁⲓ̈ (1sg suffix). The elect speaker uses this to relate the metempsychosis-fate to himself: 'if this happens against me / in my own situation.' Standard Coptic compound preposition with personal suffix.
Adverbial intensifier modifying ⲙⲁⲭϩ̄ 'hard.' Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲧⲱⲛ-stem in adverbial sense, or a doubled-form intensifier. Tentative; awaits parallels.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲙⲟⲕϩ̄ 'difficult, painful, hard.' Standard Coptic; the matter of catechumen-metempsychosis is 'exceedingly hard.'

Lycopolitan ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ- 'stand fast, be established on the feet' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast'). Used here of catechumens 'standing established in the world' before receiving faith — captures their pre-baptismal position.

proposed_english: the apostle reveals forth in the flesh
rationale: Standard Manichaean idiom for apostolic incarnational manifestation. ⲃⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (cf. ⲟ̄ⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary) here describes the apostle's self-revelation in the abiding flesh of humanity, contrasted with the soul's pre-incarnational reception of forms in the Height.
